questions.solution:

• The phrase is often used in situations where one is facing a challenge or an obstacle that seems insurmountable.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

She is laughing at me.

options.text: I am being laughed at by her.
I have been laughed by her.
I was being laughed at by her.
I had been laughed by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **I am being laughed at by her. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb is changed to the passive form "**be + past participle**."
 
• The subject of the active sentence becomes the agent (or doer) of the action in the passive sentence which is introduced by "**by**".
 
• Therefore, "**She is laughing at me**" becomes "**I am being laughed at by her**" in passive voice.

Hence, **option 1** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**I have been laughed by her**" is grammatically incorrect as it uses the wrong tense.
 
• "**I was being laughed at by he**r" is also correct but uses a different tense.
 
• "**I had been laughed by her**" is incorrect as it uses the wrong tense and implies that the laughing has already ended.
